To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new family of dinuclear zinc catalysts for the ring‐opening and copolymerization of cyclic esters, and the first example of a dinuclear zinc catalyst for CO2 insertion into aryl‐Zn bonds.

“The reactivity of di‐zinc complexes with monomers is controlled by the steric and electronic properties of both the metal and the monomer, with a balance of steric and electronic effects being required for reactivity to occur.”
“We report two new di‐zine–aryl complexes that are active in the ring opening copolymerisation reactions of CO2 with cyclohexene oxides, phthalic acid and lactides.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new catalysts based on the di‐metal centre for applications in polymer synthesis.

the synthesis and characterisation of novel zinc complexes, which are capable of catalysing ring-opening polymerisation and copolymerisation reactions, and the development of new catalytic processes for the synthesis of biodegradable polymers.
the development of new zinc‐based catalysts for CO2 insertion reactions and ring-opening polymerisation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the zinc–aryl complex, [LZinc2Ph2], is a versatile and effective polymerisation catalyst, whereas the zinc–aryl fluoride complex, [Lzinc2(C6F)2] is not.
the di‐zinc complexes are active catalysts for ring‐opening polymerisation and ring‐opening copolymersation of cyclic esters and epoxides with CO2.
the di‐zinc complex [LZnPh2] has been found to be a highly active catalyst for the ring‐opening homopolymerisation of ϵ‐capro‐lactone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the zinc–aryl bond in [LZnPh] is more reactive than the zinc–phenyl bond in [LPh2], which is more reactive than a Zn‐C6F5 bond.

the zinc–aryl complexes are not as reactive as the zinc–alkyl complexes, and the zinc–aryl complex is less reactive than the zinc‐alkyl complex in CO2 insertion, and in the polymerisation of ϵ‐capro lactone.
the di‐zinc complex [LZnPh2] is a versatile catalyst for the polymerisation of lactones and cyclic carbonates and for the copolymerisation with cyclic carbonates of epoxides and anhydrides.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the reactivity of these di‐zinc complexes with carbon dioxide can be tuned by changing the aryl group on the zinc centre, and this is a promising strategy for designing more effective CO2 insertion catalysts.
di‐zinc complexes are promising candidates for CO2 insertion and polymerisation catalysis.
di‐zinc complexes can catalyse ring‐opening polymerisation of cyclic monomers, including cyclic esters, and that the catalytic activity can be controlled by ligand substitution.
